about: Shared case table for the placement map (contract/placements.json). Every reader runs every row. readCases: reading the map file and resolving names against it; publishable says whether the strict schema accepts the file (a builder publishes only such files), read and resolve are what a tolerant reader does. sourceCases: which map a reader uses (network, last known, bundled) and with which status. showingCases: what a placement draws once its document has been loaded. Limits on the number of placements and on the published file size are publish-side only and are not rows here. The groups after showingCases are the reader rules settled after the reader audit. bodyCases: the BYTES of a map body as a reader receives them; body is a list of parts joined in order, each part is either text (encoded as UTF-8) or hex (raw bytes, two lowercase digits per byte), repeated times times (default 1); read and resolve are as in readCases. transportCases: how an HTTP answer to the map request or to the placement document request is sorted; times are milliseconds from the start of the request, headersAtMs is when the status arrives (default completedAtMs), completedAtMs is when the body ends (null: never). Document rows carry no body: a reader under test answers 2xx with any readable document. Expected for the map is the kind of the network outcome (map, corrupt, notModified, notFound, offline); for the document it is read (handed to the document reader), missing or unreadable. eventCases: settled states of one placement in order and the events the host hears; there is an event for every change of status, report, mapStatus, documentId or entry, the first settled state included. cacheCases: steps of one reader on placement home.banner of two projects (a, b) whose map and document addresses differ only in the project; map is the network outcome of the map request (the map names document d1), document is how the request for d1 ended (ok, notFound, offline); the last known map is kept per map address, and a document that answered 404 is never shown from memory again.

sourceCases.name: a readable map from the network is used and remembered
the network wins over the last known map
a fresh map without the placement is the answer: no fallback to an older map
a broken placement in a fresh map is unreadable; no fallback for one placement
304 Not Modified keeps the last known map, and it is fresh
304 without a last known map counts as no answer
304 with an unreadable last known map and nothing bundled
no answer: the last known map first
no answer and no last known map: the bundled copy
no answer and nothing to fall back on
an unreadable last known map is skipped for the bundled copy
a last known map of another major is skipped for the bundled copy
the network answered with something that is not a map: corrupt, last known map used and kept
corrupt answer and only a bundled copy
corrupt answer and nothing to fall back on
a map of another major from the network: unsupported, last known map used
another major and nothing to fall back on
404: never published and nothing to fall back on, so every placement is unknown
404 with a bundled copy: the copy shipped with the app
404 with a last known map: the same fallback order as any other failure
404 with an unreadable bundled copy: no map, and the placements are unknown

an entry and a document with no entry points

the document is gone, no entry asked

an unknown placement draws nothing and tells the host
an unreadable placement draws nothing and tells the host

bodyCases.name: the same map without a byte order mark
a UTF-8 byte order mark before the map is skipped
two byte order marks: the second one is not JSON
a byte order mark after leading whitespace is not skipped
a byte that is never UTF-8 (ff) in an unknown field spoils the whole map, it is not replaced
an overlong encoding of a slash (c0 af) in a documentId is corrupt, not a path and not a replacement character
an encoded surrogate (ed a0 80) is not UTF-8
a sequence cut short (e2 82) inside a string is not UTF-8
a code point above U+10FFFF (f4 90 80 80) is not UTF-8
a body in UTF-16 with its byte order mark is not UTF-8
valid two-, three- and four-byte sequences in an unknown field are read
32 nested arrays and objects (the root counts as one) are read
33 levels in an unknown field make the map corrupt
33 levels inside one placement make the whole map corrupt, not only that placement
33 levels of objects count the same as arrays
brackets inside strings, escaped quotes included, are not nesting
an escaped backslash ends the string before the quote, so the brackets after it count
a body of exactly 262144 bytes is read
one byte over 262144 is corrupt
the byte order mark counts toward the size limit
a major of twenty digits is another major
a major that wraps to 1 in 64 bits (2^64 + 1) is another major
a major that wraps to 1 in 32 bits (2^32 + 1) is another major
a major that a double rounds to a power of ten is another major
a minor of twenty digits is read
a patch of twenty digits is read
